newsitem.title: USA: El Paso Energy debuts expansion plan.
newsitem.headline: El Paso Energy debuts expansion plan.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp said on Wednesday that it plans to develop East Coast markets with a $350 million to $600 million expansion of its Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co subsidiary.
In the Eastern Express Project 2000, the company will be soliciting shipper interest in a non-binding open season to be held this fall for service scheduled in 2000, El Paso Energy said.
Project 2000, will include components in New England, New York City and other key markets in the northeast and southeast United States, the company said.

The retirement of nuclear power plants in New England, increased electricity demand and deregulation has led to increased activity at new power plants, El Paso said. Initially, expansion plans will target New England.
"We see a need for an incremental 400 to 500 million cubic feet a day of natural gas supplies to serve these new plants in New England," the company said in a statement.

The second component of the Eastern Express Project 2000 is an increase in capacity to serve the New York City area, the company said. Natural gas demand is expected to increase by 200 million cubic feet per day by 2000.
Tennessee Gas Pipeline is offering capacity to the markets from the Gulf of Mexico, Chicago, the Ellisburg/Leidy hub or Niagara, it said.
